notes: Scope adopted under D-T0-PROSPECTIVE-SCOPE: known development exposure, named finite suite and trusted local chronology; independence/stationarity are explicit assumptions.
Earlier candidates and original proposal remain historical evidence; no prior observations become pilot data.
Pre-pilot source repair: evaluation stops at terminal transition, preventing NaN contamination from post-terminal simulator steps. All previous development failures retained; no pilot launched.

The 46-vector reservation is the smallest ideal sufficient count for the adopted joint-event rule; all 46 must be jointly good. It is prepared, not allocated, and is not an assertion of actual workload power or practical sizing reliability.
All 258 task/phase/vector namespaces are distinct. Existing twenty-slot offsets are retained using spaced groups of pilot seeds. No workload observations were collected to choose seeds.

Evaluation now batches independent episodes, preserving per-episode keys and logical stopping. Compilation changes numerical trajectories; future scientific observations must be fresh. Serial and failed development artifacts remain unchanged.
Runtime identity now includes the exact interpreter, CUDA UUID, library paths, backend and memory fraction. The corrected CUDA path and limited memory reservation are required by fresh workers.
Task budgets, resource allocation and source/phase freeze remain incomplete. Finish the fixed final profiling plan on an allocated device before proposing a full scientific campaign.

Pre-pilot worker launch repair enforces each search/policy allowance within the remaining campaign allocation; timeout receipts are independently checked. No task/outcome/sizing change or campaign allocation.

A pilot can stop spending after search losses make even optimistic completion futile under its fixed sizing rule. All planned missing slots remain; no early success or changed confirmation rule. The prior full-study search completed nine trials; three retained development policies await an available GPU.
